board_events.text: One spot behaves as an anode, another as a cathode, with the water film as electrolyte.
Under a drop: starved centre = anode; oxygen-rich rim = cathode. Pits form at the centre.
Fe2+ is then air-oxidised to hydrated ferric oxide, the rust Fe2O3·xH2O.

segments.text: Corrosion is the villain of this chapter, a galvanic cell you never wanted. On a piece of iron exposed to moist air, one spot behaves as an anode where iron dissolves, and another as a cathode where oxygen is reduced, with the water film acting as the electrolyte.
The diagram shows the classic geometry: a single water droplet sitting on an iron surface.
That droplet sets up the whole micro-cell. One region becomes the anode, another the cathode, and the thin water film between them completes the circuit.
At the anodic spot, iron gives up electrons: solid iron becomes an iron two-plus ion plus two electrons.
At the cathodic spot, oxygen is reduced: oxygen plus hydrogen ions plus electrons give water.

<curious>Here is the beautiful detail:</curious> the metal under the centre of the drop is starved of oxygen and becomes the anode, so it dissolves, while the oxygen-rich rim becomes the cathode. Electrons travel through the metal from centre to rim, ions travel through the water. That is why pits form under a droplet, not at its edge.
Finally the iron two-plus ion is further oxidised by air to hydrated ferric oxide, which is the reddish rust, iron-three oxide with water of hydration.

Corrosion इस chapter का villain है, एक galvanic cell जो आप कभी नहीं चाहते थे। नम हवा में रखे iron के टुकड़े पर, एक spot anode की तरह behave करता है जहाँ iron घुलता है, और दूसरा cathode की तरह जहाँ oxygen reduce होता है, water film electrolyte की तरह काम करते हुए।
Diagram classic geometry दिखाता है: iron surface पर बैठी एक अकेली water droplet।
वह droplet पूरा micro-cell बना देती है। एक region anode बनता है, दूसरा cathode, और उनके बीच का पतला water film circuit complete करता है।
Anodic spot पर iron electrons देता है: solid iron बनता है एक iron two-plus ion plus दो electrons।
Cathodic spot पर oxygen reduce होता है: oxygen plus hydrogen ions plus electrons देते हैं water।

<curious>यह रही ख़ूबसूरत detail:</curious> drop के केंद्र के नीचे का metal oxygen से वंचित होकर anode बनता है, तो घुलता है, जबकि oxygen-rich rim cathode बनता है। Electrons metal से होकर केंद्र से rim तक जाते हैं, ions पानी से। इसीलिए pits droplet के नीचे बनते हैं, उसके किनारे पर नहीं।
आख़िर में iron two-plus ion हवा से और oxidise होकर hydrated ferric oxide बन जाता है, जो लाल-भूरा rust है, iron-three oxide with water of hydration।

board_events.text: Barrier coating: paint or grease keeps air and water off. Useless once scratched.
Galvanisation: a zinc layer. More reactive Zn corrodes first, even if scratched.
Sacrificial anode: bolt a Mg or Zn block; it corrodes so the structure stays cathode.
Alloying: stainless steel (iron + chromium + nickel) resists corrosion intrinsically.
Speed-ups: reactive metals, strains, impurities, salinity, acidic CO2/SO2/NO2.
Iron in a vacuum does not rust at all: the process needs both moisture and oxygen.

segments.text: Now the defences, in increasing electrochemical sophistication.
The diagram shows the two smartest ones: galvanisation with a zinc coat, and a sacrificial magnesium block bolted to the structure.
The simplest is a barrier coating: paint, grease, or a polymer just keeps air and water off the surface. It is cheap, but useless the moment it is scratched.

Next is galvanisation, coating iron with a layer of zinc. Because zinc is more reactive, with a more negative potential, even a scratched surface stays protected: the zinc preferentially corrodes and the exposed iron survives. Tin behaves oppositely, so a scratched tin can actually rusts faster.

More sophisticated is sacrificial, or cathodic, protection: you bolt a block of a more reactive metal, magnesium or zinc, to a pipeline, ship hull, or bridge. The block becomes the anode and corrodes away, forcing the protected structure to behave as the cathode. The sacrificial anode is simply replaced periodically.
The most intrinsic fix is alloying: stainless steel, iron with chromium and nickel, resists corrosion in its own right.

It also helps to know what speeds corrosion up: a more reactive metal, strains and scratches that create high-energy anodic spots, impurities that set up extra micro-cells, salinity that improves ion conduction, and acidic pollutants such as carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide, and nitrogen dioxide.
<whisper>And the clinching proof that it is electrochemical:</whisper> iron sealed in a vacuum does not rust at all. The process genuinely needs both moisture and oxygen together.
अब बचाव, बढ़ती electrochemical sophistication के क्रम में।
Diagram दो सबसे smart वाले दिखाता है: zinc coat के साथ galvanisation, और structure से bolt किया एक sacrificial magnesium block।
सबसे simple है barrier coating: paint, grease, या polymer बस हवा और पानी को surface से दूर रखता है। सस्ता है, पर scratch होते ही बेकार।

अगला है galvanisation, iron पर zinc की परत चढ़ाना। चूँकि zinc ज़्यादा reactive है, ज़्यादा negative potential के साथ, scratched surface भी protected रहता है: zinc preferentially corrode होता है और exposed iron बच जाता है। Tin उल्टा behave करता है, तो scratched tin can असल में तेज़ी से rust करता है।

ज़्यादा sophisticated है sacrificial, यानी cathodic, protection: आप एक ज़्यादा reactive metal, magnesium या zinc, का block एक pipeline, ship hull, या bridge से bolt करते हो। Block anode बनकर corrode हो जाता है, protected structure को cathode की तरह behave करने पर मजबूर करते हुए। Sacrificial anode बस समय-समय पर बदल दिया जाता है।
सबसे intrinsic fix है alloying: stainless steel, iron with chromium और nickel, अपने आप corrosion resist करता है।

यह जानना भी काम आता है कि corrosion क्या तेज़ करता है: ज़्यादा reactive metal, strains और scratches जो high-energy anodic spots बनाते हैं, impurities जो extra micro-cells बनाती हैं, salinity जो ion conduction सुधारती है, और acidic pollutants जैसे carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide, और nitrogen dioxide।
<whisper>और यह clinching proof कि यह electrochemical है:</whisper> vacuum में सील किया iron बिल्कुल rust नहीं करता। इस process को सच में moisture और oxygen दोनों साथ चाहिए।

sections.title: Faraday's-law toolkit

board_events.text: Everything the numericals rest on
$1\,F = 96500$ C = one mole of electrons = one equivalent.
For gas volumes, use electrons per molecule: 2 for H2, 4 for O2.

segments.text: Let's gather the Faraday toolkit that every electrolysis numerical uses.
First, the charge passed: charge equals current times time. Always convert the time into seconds.

Second, the master mass formula: the mass deposited equals the electrochemical equivalent times current times time, which is molar mass times current times time, all over n times the Faraday constant.

Third, the equivalent quantities: the electrochemical equivalent is molar mass over n F, which is the equivalent weight over the Faraday constant, and the equivalent weight itself is molar mass over n.
Fourth, the second law for series cells: for the same charge, the two masses are in the ratio of their equivalent weights.
Fifth, current efficiency: it is the charge actually used for the desired reaction, over the total charge passed, times one hundred percent.
Anchor the constant: one Faraday is ninety six thousand five hundred coulombs, which is one mole of electrons and exactly one equivalent.
And for gas-volume problems, the key number is the electrons per molecule: two for hydrogen, four for oxygen. That count is the whole game.
हर electrolysis numerical जिस Faraday toolkit को इस्तेमाल करती है, उसे इकट्ठा कर लेते हैं।
पहला, charge passed: charge बराबर current गुणा time। Time को हमेशा seconds में बदलो।
दूसरा, master mass formula: deposited mass बराबर electrochemical equivalent गुणा current गुणा time, यानी molar mass गुणा current गुणा time, पूरे का n गुणा Faraday constant से भाग।
तीसरा, equivalent quantities: electrochemical equivalent बराबर molar mass बटा n F, जो equivalent weight बटा Faraday constant है, और equivalent weight ख़ुद molar mass बटा n।
चौथा, series cells के लिए second law: एक ही charge के लिए, दोनों masses उनके equivalent weights के ratio में।
पाँचवाँ, current efficiency: यह desired reaction के लिए सच में इस्तेमाल हुआ charge, बटा total charge passed, गुणा one hundred percent।
Constant पक्का करो: one Faraday बराबर ninety six thousand five hundred coulombs, जो one mole electrons और exactly one equivalent है।
और gas-volume problems के लिए key number है electrons per molecule: hydrogen के लिए two, oxygen के लिए four। वही count पूरा खेल है।

segments.text: Let's start with a clean C B S E numerical. A current of two point zero amperes is passed through silver nitrate solution for thirty minutes. Find the mass of silver deposited, given the molar mass is one hundred eight and n is one.
So we have the current, the time, and the fact that silver needs just one electron. Let's work through it.
The board shows all three steps.
First convert the time: thirty minutes times sixty is one thousand eight hundred seconds.
Then the charge: current times time, two point zero times one thousand eight hundred, is three thousand six hundred coulombs.

Finally the mass: molar mass times current times time, over n times the Faraday constant. That is one hundred eight times three thousand six hundred, over one times ninety six thousand five hundred, which comes to four point zero three grams of silver.
<whisper>The trap to avoid:</whisper> always convert minutes to seconds before you compute the charge. Forgetting that is the single most common slip on this whole topic.

एक साफ़ C B S E numerical से शुरू करते हैं। Silver nitrate solution से two point zero amperes की current thirty minutes तक pass की जाती है। Deposited silver की mass निकालो, दिया है molar mass one hundred eight और n one।
तो हमारे पास current, time, और यह तथ्य है कि silver को सिर्फ़ one electron चाहिए। इसे step by step करते हैं।
Board तीनों steps दिखाता है।
पहले time convert करो: thirty minutes गुणा sixty बराबर one thousand eight hundred seconds।
फिर charge: current गुणा time, two point zero गुणा one thousand eight hundred, बराबर three thousand six hundred coulombs।

आख़िर में mass: molar mass गुणा current गुणा time, बटा n गुणा Faraday constant। यानी one hundred eight गुणा three thousand six hundred, बटा one गुणा ninety six thousand five hundred, जो आता है four point zero three grams silver।
<whisper>बचने वाला trap:</whisper> charge compute करने से पहले हमेशा minutes को seconds में बदलो। यह भूलना इस पूरे topic का सबसे आम slip है।

segments.text: Two examples that reward smart bookkeeping. First, a NEET speed trap on series cells. The same charge passes through silver nitrate and aluminium chloride in series. If one point zero eight grams of silver is deposited, what mass of aluminium is deposited?
The trap is that students compute the charge from silver, then forget that aluminium needs three electrons. Instead, work in equivalents.
The board shows both examples worked out.

Same charge means the same number of equivalents. Silver deposited is one point zero eight over one hundred eight, which is zero point zero one zero moles, and since silver is one electron, that is zero point zero one zero equivalents. So aluminium is also zero point zero one zero equivalents. The equivalent weight of aluminium is twenty seven over three, which is nine, so the mass is zero point zero one zero times nine, or zero point zero nine zero grams. No need to find the charge at all.
Now a JEE Main example on gas volumes. Acidified water is electrolysed with five point zero amperes for one thousand nine hundred thirty seconds. Find the volumes of oxygen and hydrogen at S T P.

First the charge: five point zero times one thousand nine hundred thirty is nine thousand six hundred fifty coulombs, which is zero point one zero zero Faraday, that is zero point one zero zero moles of electrons.

At the anode, oxygen takes four electrons per molecule, so the moles of oxygen are zero point one zero zero over four, which is zero point zero two five moles, giving a volume of five hundred sixty millilitres.

At the cathode, hydrogen takes two electrons per molecule, so the moles of hydrogen are zero point one zero zero over two, which is zero point zero five zero moles, giving eleven hundred twenty millilitres. The two-to-one volume ratio of hydrogen to oxygen mirrors the formula of water, a quick sanity check.

दो examples जो smart bookkeeping को reward करते हैं। पहला, series cells पर एक NEET speed trap। एक ही charge silver nitrate और aluminium chloride से series में गुज़रता है। अगर one point zero eight grams silver deposit होता है, तो कितनी mass aluminium deposit होगी?
Trap यह है कि students silver से charge compute करते हैं, फिर भूल जाते हैं कि aluminium को three electrons चाहिए। इसके बजाय equivalents में काम करो।
Board दोनों examples हल किए हुए दिखाता है।

एक ही charge मतलब एक ही संख्या के equivalents। Silver deposited बराबर one point zero eight बटा one hundred eight, यानी zero point zero one zero moles, और चूँकि silver one electron है, वह zero point zero one zero equivalents। तो aluminium भी zero point zero one zero equivalents। Aluminium का equivalent weight twenty seven बटा three, यानी nine, तो mass बराबर zero point zero one zero गुणा nine, यानी zero point zero nine zero grams। Charge निकालने की ज़रूरत ही नहीं।

अब gas volumes पर एक JEE Main example। Acidified water को five point zero amperes से one thousand nine hundred thirty seconds तक electrolyse किया जाता है। S T P पर oxygen और hydrogen के volumes निकालो।

पहले charge: five point zero गुणा one thousand nine hundred thirty बराबर nine thousand six hundred fifty coulombs, यानी zero point one zero zero Faraday, यानी zero point one zero zero moles electrons।

Anode पर oxygen हर molecule के लिए four electrons लेता है, तो oxygen के moles बराबर zero point one zero zero बटा four, यानी zero point zero two five moles, जिससे volume five hundred sixty millilitres।

Cathode पर hydrogen हर molecule के लिए two electrons लेता है, तो hydrogen के moles बराबर zero point one zero zero बटा two, यानी zero point zero five zero moles, जिससे eleven hundred twenty millilitres। Hydrogen और oxygen का two-to-one volume ratio पानी के formula को दर्शाता है, एक quick sanity check।

segments.text: Now a full JEE Advanced problem combining series cells with current efficiency. Two electrolytic cells, one with molten aluminium chloride and one with aqueous copper sulphate, are connected in series. After some time, one point two seven grams of copper is deposited. Find the mass of aluminium, the time if the current was two amperes, and the current efficiency if the aluminium actually deposited was zero point three two four grams.
Copper's molar mass is sixty three point five with n equal to two; aluminium's is twenty seven with n equal to three. The board walks all the parts.

First the charge from copper. Moles of copper are one point two seven over sixty three point five, which is zero point zero two zero zero moles. The charge is n times moles times the Faraday constant: two times zero point zero two zero zero times ninety six thousand five hundred, which is three thousand eight hundred sixty coulombs.

For part a, the same charge flows through the series, so the moles of aluminium are the charge over three times the Faraday constant, which is zero point zero one three three three moles. The mass is that times twenty seven, giving zero point three six zero grams.
For part b, the time is the charge over the current: three thousand eight hundred sixty over two point zero, which is one thousand nine hundred thirty seconds, about thirty two minutes.

For part c, the current efficiency is the actual mass over the theoretical mass, times one hundred: zero point three two four over zero point three six zero, times one hundred, which is ninety percent.

<curious>What happened to the missing ten percent?</curious> That charge went into side-reactions, such as some hydrogen evolution, and that is exactly the real-world departure from Faraday's idealisation of one hundred percent efficiency.

अब एक full JEE Advanced problem जो series cells को current efficiency के साथ जोड़ता है। दो electrolytic cells, एक molten aluminium chloride वाली और एक aqueous copper sulphate वाली, series में जुड़ी हैं। कुछ समय बाद one point two seven grams copper deposit होता है। Aluminium की mass, current two amperes होने पर time, और aluminium actually zero point three two four grams deposit होने पर current efficiency निकालो।
Copper का molar mass sixty three point five, n बराबर two; aluminium का twenty seven, n बराबर three। Board सारे parts चलता है।

पहले copper से charge। Copper के moles बराबर one point two seven बटा sixty three point five, यानी zero point zero two zero zero moles। Charge बराबर n गुणा moles गुणा Faraday constant: two गुणा zero point zero two zero zero गुणा ninety six thousand five hundred, यानी three thousand eight hundred sixty coulombs।

Part a के लिए, वही charge series से बहता है, तो aluminium के moles बराबर charge बटा three गुणा Faraday constant, यानी zero point zero one three three three moles। Mass बराबर उसका twenty seven गुना, यानी zero point three six zero grams।
Part b के लिए, time बराबर charge बटा current: three thousand eight hundred sixty बटा two point zero, यानी one thousand nine hundred thirty seconds, करीब thirty two minutes।
Part c के लिए, current efficiency बराबर actual mass बटा theoretical mass, गुणा one hundred: zero point three two four बटा zero point three six zero, गुणा one hundred, यानी ninety percent।

<curious>ग़ायब ten percent का क्या हुआ?</curious> वह charge side-reactions में गया, जैसे कुछ hydrogen evolution, और यही Faraday के one hundred percent efficiency वाले idealisation से real-world का फ़र्क़ है।

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips for electrolysis

board_events.text: Where marks slip in electrolysis
Minutes vs seconds: $Q=It$ needs $t$ in seconds. The most frequent error.
Dropping $n$: the formula is $W=\frac{MIt}{nF}$, not $\frac{MIt}{F}$.
Electrolytic polarity is opposite to galvanic: anode $+$, cathode $-$.
Always include water (H2O, H+, OH-) as candidate species in aqueous electrolysis.
Pro-tip: for series cells, think in equivalents, not coulombs.
For gas volumes, the electrons-per-molecule count (2 for H2, 4 for O2) is the whole game.

segments.text: Let's close this subtopic with the traps that quietly cost marks in electrolysis.
First and most frequent: minutes versus seconds. The charge equals current times time formula needs the time in seconds. Forgetting to convert minutes or hours is the number-one numerical error here.

Second, dropping n. The mass formula is molar mass times current times time, over n times the Faraday constant. Students who use it without the n overstate copper, aluminium, and the rest. Always read n off the balanced electrode reaction.
Third, polarity. In an electrolytic cell the anode is positive and the cathode is negative, the opposite of a galvanic cell. Mixing the two conventions is a guaranteed mark-loss.

Fourth, forgetting water. In aqueous electrolysis, always include water and its ions as candidate species, and remember that overpotential can override the electrode-potential prediction, which is why aqueous sodium chloride gives chlorine, not oxygen.

<whisper>Now the pro-tips that save real time.</whisper> For series-cell problems, think in equivalents, not coulombs. The same charge means the same number of equivalents in every cell, so the mass ratio equals the equivalent-weight ratio, and you get the answer in one line.
And for gas-volume problems, the electrons-per-molecule count is the whole game: two for hydrogen, four for oxygen. Nail that count and the volumes fall out immediately.
Electrolysis में चुपचाप marks ले जाने वाले traps के साथ इस subtopic को close करते हैं।
पहला और सबसे आम: minutes बनाम seconds। Charge बराबर current गुणा time वाले formula को time seconds में चाहिए। Minutes या hours convert करना भूलना यहाँ number-one numerical error है।

दूसरा, n छोड़ना। Mass formula है molar mass गुणा current गुणा time, बटा n गुणा Faraday constant। जो इसे n के बिना इस्तेमाल करते हैं वे copper, aluminium वगैरह को ज़्यादा बता देते हैं। हमेशा balanced electrode reaction से n पढ़ो।
तीसरा, polarity। Electrolytic cell में anode positive और cathode negative, galvanic cell से उल्टा। दोनों conventions mix करना guaranteed mark-loss है।

चौथा, पानी भूलना। Aqueous electrolysis में हमेशा water और उसके ions को candidate species में शामिल करो, और याद रखो कि overpotential electrode-potential prediction को override कर सकता है, इसीलिए aqueous sodium chloride chlorine देता है, oxygen नहीं।

<whisper>अब वे pro-tips जो सच में time बचाते हैं।</whisper> Series-cell problems के लिए equivalents में सोचो, coulombs में नहीं। एक ही charge मतलब हर cell में एक ही संख्या के equivalents, तो mass ratio बराबर equivalent-weight ratio, और answer एक line में मिल जाता है।
और gas-volume problems के लिए electrons-per-molecule count पूरा खेल है: hydrogen के लिए two, oxygen के लिए four। वह count पक्का करो और volumes तुरंत निकल आते हैं।

Both half-cells identical, so $E^\circ_{cell}=0$: the whole emf is the log term.

segments.text: Every cell so far paired two different electrodes. But you can build a working cell from two identical electrodes dipping in solutions of the same ion at different concentrations. That is a concentration cell.

There is no chemical difference between the two sides at all. The only driving force is the concentration gap, exactly like gas rushing from high pressure to low. Nature wants the two concentrations equal.
Here is a zinc example: one zinc rod in dilute zinc ions, one in concentrated zinc ions, joined by a salt bridge.
The diagram makes it concrete, with the dilute beaker on the left and the concentrated on the right.
The concentrated side is reduced and becomes the cathode: its surplus ions plate out. The dilute side is oxidised and becomes the anode: its rod dissolves to top up the ions.

<curious>Now here is the elegant part.</curious> Because both half-cells are chemically identical, the standard potentials cancel exactly, so the standard cell potential is zero. The entire e m f comes from the Nernst log term alone.
And the cell runs until the two concentrations become equal, at which point there is no gap left to drive it, and it is dead.

अब तक हर cell ने दो अलग electrodes को जोड़ा। पर आप एक working cell दो identical electrodes से भी बना सकते हो, जो एक ही ion के अलग-अलग concentrations वाले solutions में डूबे हों। यही concentration cell है।
दोनों sides में कोई chemical अंतर है ही नहीं। एकमात्र driving force है concentration gap, बिल्कुल जैसे gas high pressure से low की ओर दौड़ती है। Nature दोनों concentrations बराबर चाहती है।
यह रहा एक zinc example: एक zinc rod dilute zinc ions में, एक concentrated zinc ions में, एक salt bridge से जुड़े।
Diagram इसे concrete बना देता है, left पर dilute beaker और right पर concentrated।
Concentrated side reduce होकर cathode बनता है: उसके अतिरिक्त ions plate out हो जाते हैं। Dilute side oxidise होकर anode बनता है: उसका rod घुलकर ions की भरपाई करता है।

<curious>अब यह रहा elegant हिस्सा।</curious> चूँकि दोनों half-cells chemically identical हैं, standard potentials exactly cancel हो जाते हैं, तो standard cell potential zero है। पूरा e m f अकेले Nernst log term से आता है।
और cell तब तक चलती है जब तक दोनों concentrations बराबर न हो जाएँ, जिस बिंदु पर इसे चलाने के लिए कोई gap नहीं बचता, और यह dead है।

board_events.text: Since $c_2$ (cathode) $> c_1$ (anode), the log is positive and $E_{cell}>0$.

segments.text: Let's derive the working formula. Start from the Nernst equation and simply set the standard cell potential to zero, since we just saw it vanishes.
What remains is beautifully simple: the cell potential equals zero point zero five nine one over n, times the log of the cathode concentration over the anode concentration.
For the cell to be spontaneous, the cathode concentration must be larger than the anode concentration, so that the log is positive.
The diagram shows the derivation and, importantly, what happens to the emf over time.

Trace it through: for the net process taking zinc ions from the concentrated side to the dilute side, the Nernst equation gives zero minus the constant times log of c-one over c-two, which flips to the constant times log of c-two over c-one.
Since the concentrated cathode concentration exceeds the dilute anode concentration, that log is positive and the cell potential is positive, exactly as a spontaneous cell should be.
<whisper>One thing to expect on the exam:</whisper> the e m f here is small, typically only millivolts, and it shrinks steadily to zero as the two concentrations converge.
Working formula derive करते हैं। Nernst equation से शुरू करो और बस standard cell potential को zero रख दो, क्योंकि हमने अभी देखा कि वह ग़ायब हो जाता है।
जो बचता है वह ख़ूबसूरती से simple है: cell potential बराबर zero point zero five nine one over n, गुणा cathode concentration बटा anode concentration का log।
Cell के spontaneous होने के लिए cathode concentration, anode concentration से बड़ी होनी चाहिए, ताकि log positive हो।
Diagram derivation दिखाता है और, ख़ास तौर पर, समय के साथ emf का क्या होता है।

इसे trace करो: zinc ions को concentrated side से dilute side ले जाने वाले net process के लिए, Nernst equation देता है zero minus constant गुणा c-one over c-two का log, जो पलटकर constant गुणा c-two over c-one बन जाता है।
चूँकि concentrated cathode concentration, dilute anode concentration से ज़्यादा है, वह log positive है और cell potential positive, ठीक जैसा एक spontaneous cell को होना चाहिए।
<whisper>Exam पर एक बात expect करो:</whisper> यहाँ e m f छोटा होता है, आम तौर पर सिर्फ़ millivolts, और यह लगातार zero तक सिकुड़ता है जैसे-जैसे दोनों concentrations पास आती हैं।

segments.text: Let's put the formula to work on three problems, from a plain emf to reverse-engineering a concentration.

Example A, at C B S E level. A zinc concentration cell has the dilute side at zero point zero zero one molar and the concentrated side at zero point one zero molar, with n equal to two. Find the e m f.

The cathode is the higher concentration, so the cell potential is zero point zero five nine one over two, times the log of zero point one zero over zero point zero zero one. That log is log of one hundred, which is two, so the answer is zero point zero five nine one volts.
The board shows all three examples side by side.
Example B, at JEE Main level. A copper concentration cell has the cathode at one point zero molar and develops an e m f of zero point zero two nine five volts. Find the anode concentration.

Set zero point zero two nine five equal to zero point zero five nine one over two, times the log of one point zero over the anode concentration. The log must equal one, so one point zero over the concentration is ten, giving an anode concentration of zero point one zero molar.

Example C, at JEE Advanced level. A silver concentration cell with n equal to one has an e m f of zero point one one eight volts, with the known side at one point zero molar. Find the unknown concentration x, and say what happens as the cell discharges.

Here zero point one one eight equals zero point zero five nine one times the log of one point zero over x, so the log is two and x is zero point zero one molar. <chuckle>And the trend:</chuckle> as the cell runs, the dilute side grows more concentrated while the one-molar side is diluted, so the ratio approaches one, the log approaches zero, and the e m f falls to zero. The concentration cell dies when the two sides equalise.
Formula को तीन problems पर लगाते हैं, एक plain emf से लेकर एक concentration को reverse-engineer करने तक।
Example A, C B S E level पर। एक zinc concentration cell में dilute side zero point zero zero one molar और concentrated side zero point one zero molar है, n बराबर two। E m f निकालो।

Cathode ज़्यादा concentration वाला है, तो cell potential बराबर zero point zero five nine one over two, गुणा zero point one zero over zero point zero zero one का log। वह log है log of one hundred, यानी two, तो answer है zero point zero five nine one volts।
Board तीनों examples साथ-साथ दिखाता है।
Example B, JEE Main level पर। एक copper concentration cell में cathode one point zero molar है और e m f zero point zero two nine five volts बनाता है। Anode concentration निकालो।

Zero point zero two nine five को zero point zero five nine one over two, गुणा one point zero over anode concentration के log के बराबर रखो। Log एक होना चाहिए, तो one point zero over concentration दस है, जिससे anode concentration zero point one zero molar।

Example C, JEE Advanced level पर। n बराबर one वाली एक silver concentration cell का e m f zero point one one eight volts है, known side one point zero molar पर। Unknown concentration x निकालो, और बताओ कि cell discharge होते समय क्या होता है।

यहाँ zero point one one eight बराबर zero point zero five nine one गुणा one point zero over x का log, तो log two है और x zero point zero one molar। <chuckle>और trend:</chuckle> जैसे-जैसे cell चलती है, dilute side ज़्यादा concentrated होती जाती है जबकि one-molar side dilute होती है, तो ratio one की ओर बढ़ता है, log zero की ओर, और e m f zero तक गिरता है। Concentration cell तब मरती है जब दोनों sides बराबर हो जाती हैं।

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips for concentration cells

board_events.text: The traps unique to concentration cells
The concentrated electrode is the CATHODE (reduced); the dilute one is the anode.
$E^\circ_{cell}=0$ because both half-cells are identical: never plug a nonzero $E^\circ$.
The emf is small (millivolts) and falls to $0$ as the sides converge.
A concentration cell exists only to average out a concentration imbalance.
Pro-tip: put the larger concentration on top of the log to keep $E_{cell}>0$.
As it discharges, dilute side rises, concentrated side drops, ratio $\to 1$, emf $\to 0$.

segments.text: Let's close concentration cells with the traps that are unique to them.
First and most common: the concentrated electrode is the cathode, where reduction happens, and the dilute electrode is the anode. Students often swap these, which flips the sign.
Second, remember that the standard cell potential is exactly zero here, because both half-cells are chemically identical. Never plug a nonzero standard potential into the formula.
Third, expect a small answer. The e m f of a concentration cell is only millivolts, and it falls to zero as the two sides converge, so a large answer signals an error.
Fourth, keep the physical picture in mind: a concentration cell exists purely to average out a concentration imbalance. That intuition tells you the direction every time.

<whisper>Here is the pro-tip that prevents sign errors:</whisper> always put the larger concentration on top of the log ratio, the cathode over the anode, and the cell potential comes out positive automatically.

And finally, track the trend as it discharges: the dilute side rises, the concentrated side drops, the ratio approaches one, and the e m f approaches zero. That is the whole life story of a concentration cell.
Concentration cells को उन traps के साथ close करते हैं जो सिर्फ़ इन्हीं के हैं।
पहला और सबसे आम: concentrated electrode cathode है, जहाँ reduction होता है, और dilute electrode anode। Students अक्सर इन्हें उलट देते हैं, जिससे sign flip हो जाता है।
दूसरा, याद रखो कि यहाँ standard cell potential exactly zero है, क्योंकि दोनों half-cells chemically identical हैं। Formula में कभी nonzero standard potential मत डालो।
तीसरा, छोटा answer expect करो। Concentration cell का e m f सिर्फ़ millivolts होता है, और दोनों sides के पास आते ही zero तक गिरता है, तो बड़ा answer error का संकेत है।
चौथा, physical picture दिमाग़ में रखो: concentration cell सिर्फ़ एक concentration imbalance को average out करने के लिए मौजूद होती है। वह intuition हर बार direction बता देती है।
<whisper>यह रहा वह pro-tip जो sign errors रोकता है:</whisper> हमेशा बड़ी concentration को log ratio के ऊपर रखो, cathode बटा anode, और cell potential अपने आप positive आता है।
और आख़िर में, discharge होते समय trend track करो: dilute side बढ़ती है, concentrated side गिरती है, ratio one की ओर, और e m f zero की ओर। यही concentration cell की पूरी जीवन-कहानी है।

sections.title: Complete chapter formula recap

board_events.text: Your complete Electrochemistry toolkit
That is your complete toolkit: cells, Nernst, conductance, and Faraday, all on one board.

segments.text: Here is your complete toolkit for the whole chapter, gathered on one board. This is a recap, so I will restate each relation rather than re-teach it.
First, cells and thermodynamics: the standard cell potential is cathode minus anode, and the standard Gibbs energy is minus n F times that potential.

Second, Nernst and equilibrium: the cell potential is the standard potential minus zero point zero five nine one over n times log Q, and log of K c is n times the standard potential over zero point zero five nine one.
Third, the concentration cell: the cell potential is zero point zero five nine one over n, times the log of the cathode concentration over the anode concentration.
Fourth, conductance: conductance is one over resistance, conductivity is conductance times the cell constant, and molar conductivity is kappa times one thousand over the molarity.

Fifth, strong and weak electrolytes: the square-root law for the strong ones, and for the weak ones the degree of dissociation is molar conductivity over the limiting value, with the dissociation constant c alpha squared over one minus alpha.

Sixth, Faraday's laws: charge is current times time, mass is molar mass times current times time over n F, series masses are in the ratio of equivalent weights, and one Faraday is ninety six thousand five hundred coulombs.
That is the entire chapter, from galvanic cells to Faraday's laws, distilled onto a single board. Keep this in front of you for every numerical.
यह रहा पूरे chapter के लिए आपका complete toolkit, एक board पर इकट्ठा। यह एक recap है, तो मैं हर relation को दोबारा पढ़ाने के बजाय बस restate करूँगा।
पहला, cells और thermodynamics: standard cell potential बराबर cathode minus anode, और standard Gibbs energy बराबर minus n F गुणा वह potential।

दूसरा, Nernst और equilibrium: cell potential बराबर standard potential minus zero point zero five nine one over n गुणा log Q, और K c का log बराबर n गुणा standard potential बटा zero point zero five nine one।
तीसरा, concentration cell: cell potential बराबर zero point zero five nine one over n, गुणा cathode concentration बटा anode concentration का log।
चौथा, conductance: conductance बराबर one over resistance, conductivity बराबर conductance गुणा cell constant, और molar conductivity बराबर kappa गुणा one thousand बटा molarity।

पाँचवाँ, strong और weak electrolytes: strong के लिए square-root law, और weak के लिए degree of dissociation बराबर molar conductivity बटा limiting value, dissociation constant c alpha squared बटा one minus alpha के साथ।

छठा, Faraday's laws: charge बराबर current गुणा time, mass बराबर molar mass गुणा current गुणा time बटा n F, series masses equivalent weights के ratio में, और one Faraday बराबर ninety six thousand five hundred coulombs।
यही पूरा chapter है, galvanic cells से Faraday's laws तक, एक ही board पर निचोड़ा हुआ। हर numerical के लिए इसे सामने रखो।

segments.text: Finally, the whole chapter compressed onto one page for the night before the exam. Quick recall, no explanations.
Galvanic cell: the anode is oxidation and is negative, the cathode is reduction and is positive, and electrons flow from anode to cathode.
Notation: anode on the left, cathode on the right; a single bar is a phase boundary, a double bar is the salt bridge.
A dead cell means the cell potential is zero and the reaction quotient equals the equilibrium constant, and remember that is not the same as the standard potential being zero.

Keep this master reference in view: the key electrode potentials, from fluorine at the top to lithium at the bottom, the common products of electrolysis, and the anomalously high hydrogen and hydroxide ionic conductivities.
On dilution, kappa drops while molar conductivity lifts. Molten sodium chloride gives sodium and chlorine; aqueous sodium chloride gives hydrogen, chlorine, and sodium hydroxide.
Corrosion needs both water and oxygen, and you prevent it by galvanisation with zinc or by a sacrificial magnesium or zinc anode.

And the memory aids to carry in: An Ox, Red Cat, for anode oxidation and reduction cathode; in electrolysis the positive electrode is the anode; and one mole of electrons is one equivalent and ninety six thousand five hundred coulombs. You are ready for this chapter.
आख़िर में, पूरा chapter exam से एक रात पहले के लिए एक page पर निचोड़ा हुआ। Quick recall, कोई explanation नहीं।
Galvanic cell: anode oxidation है और negative, cathode reduction है और positive, और electrons anode से cathode की ओर बहते हैं।
Notation: anode left पर, cathode right पर; single bar phase boundary है, double bar salt bridge।
Dead cell का मतलब cell potential zero और reaction quotient बराबर equilibrium constant, और याद रखो यह standard potential zero होने जैसा नहीं है।
यह master reference सामने रखो: key electrode potentials, ऊपर fluorine से नीचे lithium तक, electrolysis के common products, और anomalously high hydrogen और hydroxide ionic conductivities।
Dilution पर kappa गिरता है जबकि molar conductivity चढ़ती है। Molten sodium chloride देता है sodium और chlorine; aqueous sodium chloride देता है hydrogen, chlorine, और sodium hydroxide।
Corrosion को water और oxygen दोनों चाहिए, और आप इसे zinc से galvanisation या एक sacrificial magnesium या zinc anode से रोकते हो।

और साथ ले जाने वाली memory aids: An Ox, Red Cat, यानी anode oxidation और reduction cathode; electrolysis में positive electrode anode है; और one mole electrons बराबर one equivalent और ninety six thousand five hundred coulombs। आप इस chapter के लिए तैयार हो।
